findings.title: Retention as protection from entrusted abandonment
findings.claim: The focus promise can also describe the received recitation as being kept from deliberate abandonment: the recitation is delivered, and the entrusted word remains in use rather than being left aside.
findings.mechanism: The focus n-s-y form is the carrier. The supplied 20:126 and 9:67 scenes provide independent cases where forgetting functions as leaving received signs or an entrusted relation, so the focus negation changes the result from memory-only protection to continued keeping of a charge.
findings.reader_payoff: The promise covers what happens to received material after it has been given: it stays active in conduct, not merely present in recollection.
findings.containment: The ordinary promise about not forgetting remains intact; this added ethical and behavioral sense concerns the use of the received recitation and does not claim that every forgetting occurrence means deliberate abandonment.

epistemic.reason: A trusted publication and an accepted focus branch ground the claim; the external connection cards supply exact target surfaces but omit target morphology, so the cross-ayah reinforcement remains qualified.
